summary.text: A 26-year-old man had fluctuating paranoid-hallucinatory symptoms since age 20 and was followed up for schizophrenia for about 3 years, with paranoid schizophrenia diagnosed by multiple psychiatrists. Despite neuroleptics he had 4 exacerbation episodes of several weeks with thought disorder, persecutory delusions and auditory, visual and tactile hallucinations, with severe negative and cognitive symptoms. No family history of neurological or psychological illness was identified.

He had been treated with amisulpride, benperidol, chlorprothixene, levomepromazine, olanzapine and clozapine at standard doses for an adequate period without proper response. Treatment-resistant schizophrenia was diagnosed and M-ECT was started. Before ECT he had clear deficits in almost every PSYRATS subscale.

He received a series of ECT sessions and a course of 24 treatments over 1 year, bilateral under general anesthesia, initially weekly, later every second week and then monthly. Olanzapine 10 mg morning and night stayed unchanged, and no add-on psychiatric in-house treatment was needed during the M-ECT course.

After 24 ECT sessions symptom severity was much weaker and limited to some PSYRATS subscales, and the total and subscale PSYRATS scores changed for the better. The authors report improved positive and negative symptoms, psychotic symptoms that remained stable over the M-ECT course, good tolerance and compliance, and no significant side effects or reported side effects such as memory impairment.
